classification.difficultyReason: Trace the exposed folded boundary, exclude internal lines and use Pythagoras for the two diagonal edges before adding lengths.

content.prompt: A rectangular strip of paper has dimensions $5$ cm by $1$ cm. It is folded into the figure shown below. Find the perimeter of this figure.

spec.description: Three squares rise from lower left to upper right with two triangular connecting regions, complete internal fold edges, equal-length ticks and two right-angle markers. Decorative blue fills are omitted; fold boundaries retain the piece relationships.
spec.mathematics: Ticked edges have common length 1 cm. The exposed outline contains eight unit edges and two diagonals of unit right triangles.
spec.answerVisibility: No unit labels, diagonal lengths or perimeter answer are added to the question figure.

answer.short:
$(8+2\sqrt2)\,\mathrm{cm}$

Count eight exposed unit edges and two unit-square diagonals.
answer.worked:
Each ticked segment is $1$ cm, the width of the strip. Each diagonal boundary has length
$$\begin{align*}d&=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}\\d&=\sqrt2\,\mathrm{cm}.\end{align*}$$
There are eight exposed unit edges and two diagonal edges.
$$\begin{align*}P&=8\times1+2\sqrt2\\P&=(8+2\sqrt2)\,\mathrm{cm}.\end{align*}$$
